Overlap length computation

I find the current problem description sufficiently clear. Perhaps a minor correction: "You are given [[n]] shards, where the [[i]]-th shard has [[m_i]] vertices."
Please also state that [[shard1]] and [[shard2]] are 1-indexed.

I found it helpful to visualize the shards in Desmos geometry calculator: https://imgur.com/a/e9n04Mj. This could at least give the player some idea of where to start in solving the jigsaw-like puzzle.

Not sure if possible to provide some visual help (not sure if we can add some screenshot or maybe a some sort of ascii art representation of frames and shards)
I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!

I don't even know where to start with this one...
Probably why this is very hard difficulty.

Goal
* Please correct the typos:
  • accidentaly => accidentally
  • milimetres => millimetres

* 1st sentence: Please change "12×12cm square sheet of glass" to "frame".

* 2nd sentence: Consider changing ", which resulted in him dropping" to "and dropped".

* 2nd sentence: Please change "the sheet of glass" to "the frame, shattering the 12cm x 12cm sheet of glass inside".

* Please change "various rotations" to "various orientations" (there are 2 such instances; don't change other instances of "rotation(s)").

* 3rd paragraph: Please change "12x12cm" to "12cm x 12cm".

* 3rd paragraph: Please change "final solve" to "final solution". Better yet, change "in the final solve" to "when reassembled".

* Please change "nor mirroring" to "or flipping" (change both words).

Input
* Line 1: Please change "clarifying" to "indicating".

* Line 2: Please change "depicting" to "specifying".

* Next n lines: Please change "clarifying" to "indicating".

* Next p lines: Please add "its" before "corresponding".

* Please add a note:

Note: The vertices are given in the same order as the number of vertices listed for each shard. That is, if the [[n]] lines specify [[m₁]], [[m₂]], ..., [[mₙ]] vertices, then the first [[m₁]] vertex lines belong to the first shard, the next [[m₂]] to the second shard, and so on.

Output
* Please add "are" between "that" and "between".

* Please change "zero" to "{{0.000}}".

Constraints
* Please change "are possible" to "are solvable".

Cases / Solution code
* Please change the expected output of all cases to always show 3 decimal places (e.g. 0.000 instead of 0.0).

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement.

Cases
* Please delete the trailing newlines from the input of all the cases.

Cover picture
* Consider uploading a cover picture for the puzzle.

Thanks.

Hi!
Now I didn't expect an English teacher to comment, but I changed it like you wanted because I'm not much good at writing and English isn't my first language. The cover picture is to be done, as well as a few more test cases.

Well, it looks like not many people are interested in solving this, so not really, I don't have much progress on submitting it.

I'm planning to provide images of all the test cases (not validators of course) in a google doc, both in the unsolved and solved case, but that's still in the making. I haven't had the time to work on this for a few weeks anyways.

If you have any ideas about how I could make the goal more clear, please tell me what you don't understand and how I could change it. Thanks!

Hi!

Thank you for taking the time to go through the suggestions and implement them. Just to clarify, some of the comments on the language were meant to help make the problem easier to understand. They weren't intended as language corrections for the sake of it.

Here's a recap of the remaining points:

Goal
* 2nd paragraph: Please change "rotations" to "orientations".

Cases
* Pending review after you've added them.

Cover picture
* Pending.

Thanks again.
I know and I'm fine with it. By the way, are you a mod that you always give these "corrections" under every new contribution? I don't mean it in a bad way, just curious.

I'm fine with your question 🙂

I'm a moderator, but my responsibilities don't include making suggestions on every new contribution. In fact, anyone is welcome to offer suggestions if they wish to help.

Personally, I believe
(a) It's better to catch and address issues before a contribution is approved, rather than after.

(b) A well-polished submission is more likely to be accepted and ultimately leads to a better experience for everyone, especially for those who solve a clash/puzzle with the aim to practise programming.

That's what motivates me to review and provide feedback on each new contribution.
I'm actually impressed that you take the time to read through each and every one of them. But I shouldn't be surprised since you have solved basically every puzzle on this platform.
Thank you for your kind words!

I've reviewed the current test cases, and they look good to me. I haven't tried solving the puzzle myself, so somebody who does may spot issues that I might have missed.

From my side, the only remaining item is the cover picture for the puzzle, unless you're planning to add more test cases.

Thanks.
